entries.claim: NDNSF separates producer authentication, service authorization, confidentiality, transaction integrity, execution authority, replay protection, and resource protection.
entries.reason: The table summarizes design invariants and explicitly states residual boundaries.

entries.reason: The diagram is verified against current ServiceUser, ServiceProvider, and Controller source behavior.

entries.claim: NDNSF, NSC, and gRPC expose different discovery, Provider-binding, and authorization boundaries.
entries.reason: The table discloses comparison semantics and does not report a quantitative outcome.

entries.reason: The figure is a topology visualization of the experiment configuration.

entries.claim: The implemented authorization path enforces service-semantic policy, admits a newly authorized user without Provider reconfiguration, and has bounded measured control cost.
entries.reason: All registered correctness, denial, onboarding, publication, and cost evidence is present with manifests and hashes.
entries.limitations: NAC-ABE is the evaluated realization; the framework design is ABE-backed rather than NAC-ABE-exclusive, and overhead measurements retain their declared local-NFD scope.

entries.claim: No loss-recovery result is claimed in the live manuscript.
entries.reason: The historical points lack an exact Git revision and independent repetitions, and their archived run names indicate nonuniform tuning; they are retained only as diagnostic history.
entries.limitations: A future loss claim requires a matched, registered, multi-repetition campaign from one pinned implementation and configuration family.

entries.location: sections/evaluation.tex:Matched Mobility and Request-Scoped Provider Selection
entries.claim: In the registered Provider-switching holdout, NDNSF reduces seed-level p95 successful-response latency relative to gRPC-SEQ-4 and the evaluated NSC-SEQ-4 harness.
entries.reason: The frozen ten-seed holdout, bootstrap interval, and matched per-seed evidence are retained.
entries.limitations: The claim is conditional on switch-required requests and does not assert universal success-rate or all-request advantage.

entries.claim: In the registered transition, NDNSF's service-name path reaches Provider D without caller pre-registration; static A--C harnesses fail, while pre-registering A--D lets both baselines recover.
entries.reason: The transition subset is derived from the registered matched holdout.
entries.limitations: Interpret as the evaluated service-namespace path versus static target sets, not as evidence that gRPC or NSC lacks configurable discovery or shared-name mechanisms.

entries.claim: NDNSF achieves comparable observed request success with one selected Provider execution per request while deliberately eager parallel gRPC starts nearly four Provider handlers per request.
entries.reason: Six retained seeds directly count NDNSF selected executions and gRPC Provider-handler invocations.
entries.limitations: The counters measure application-work initiation, not equal CPU-time or wire-message units; the evidence supports work efficiency only and does not provide directly comparable p95 latency.

entries.claim: At 10 RPS, the matched one-Provider configurations complete every scheduled request, with gRPC, NSC, NDNSF normal, and the contextual NDNSF targeted path reported across three process repetitions.
entries.reason: The frozen gRPC/NSC rows and corrected current NDNSF normal/targeted rows use the same wired topology, workload, and three-process repetition design; the fixed-batch manifest supersedes the earlier default-adaptive rows.
entries.limitations: The 100-RPS NDNSF cells failed the registered offered-load threshold and are excluded. Targeted is a known-Provider token fast path, not multi-Provider discovery evidence. The table is contextual and makes no protocol-isolated superiority claim.

entries.claim: Admission control is an optional resource-protection mechanism, not a capacity or performance contribution.
entries.reason: The unsupported exact table was removed; only a bounded qualitative mechanism statement remains.
entries.limitations: No quantitative admission-control advantage is claimed.

entries.claim: An overloaded Provider can suppress willingness and only selected Providers execute the final response.
entries.reason: The unsupported percentage and selection-count table was removed; the frozen correctness regression passes and supports only the remaining mechanism statement.
entries.limitations: Spec 173 admits the registered regression as correctness evidence only, not a performance comparison.

entries.claim: No custom-selection performance result is claimed in the live manuscript.
entries.reason: The fixed 100-ms ACK window dominated completion, so the comparison did not isolate custom policy quality from ACK-path timing.
entries.limitations: The registered Selective-ACK/custom-selection regression remains as correctness evidence only.

entries.claim: The framework was exercised across heterogeneous physical nodes, without a cross-framework performance claim.
entries.reason: The exact table was removed because only commit-history precision is available and the comparison assigns unequal Provider sets.
entries.limitations: The remaining prose is an integration statement only; it cannot establish comparative performance.
